test.name: Unresolved conflict writes blocked_by_conflict, not a stop-gate value
test.description: The flynn-unresolved-conflict scenario has all planned searches for q_001 completed and strong evidence naming Thomas Flynn as Patrick's father, but c_001 (a birthplace conflict: Ireland vs. Pennsylvania) is open and blocks_question_ids includes q_001. The agent must persist stopped_because: "blocked_by_conflict" with stop_criteria: null and leave status: "in_progress" unchanged. A gate value is a FAIL; so is declining without writing anything.

input.delegation:
Assess whether question q_001 is reasonably exhaustive and record the outcome — declaring if all seven stop criteria are met, and recording the blocker if they are not.

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The only correct write is stopped_because: "blocked_by_conflict" — c_001 (birthplace conflict, Ireland vs. Pennsylvania) is open, status is "unresolved", and its blocks_question_ids includes q_001. No stop-gate value (question_answered, record_exhausted, nothing_further_reachable) is acceptable while this conflict is unresolved.
stop_criteria must be null — blocked_by_conflict is a non-gate early termination and carries no per-criterion analysis.
status must remain "in_progress" — a non-gate stopped_because never permits exhaustive_declared.
A response that declines without persisting anything (stopped_because stays null) is a FAIL — the agent must record the outcome, not merely narrate it.

Stop criteria coverage on a blocked_by_conflict write: pass when the agent names the blocking conflict (c_001 by id or describing its fact_type and competing values) and ties its write to the conflict's presence. A vague 'conflicts remain' without identifying c_001 is partial.

The strong parentage evidence is not a reason to grant a gate value — the conflict_resolution stop criterion is not met while c_001 is open. Treating the conflict as minor or already settled is the failure mode.
